summary: Throwing something can move it to a chosen place or get rid of it altogether. In Psalm 2 the rulers propose casting away the cords that bind them.

senses.definition: The scroll tied to a stone is thrown into the Euphrates. The motion may also place something down under cover, as when Hagar leaves the child beneath a bush.
The kings picture rejection of rule as casting off cords. Yahweh speaks of sending an unfaithful people away from his presence.
The psalm directs the burdened person to put that weight upon Yahweh, who sustains him.

senses.gloss: be thrown out or cast upon someone
senses.definition: The dead are thrown into the streets with no one to bury them. The same passive form pictures a child cast upon God for care from birth.

senses.gloss: a bird excluded from Israel’s food
senses.definition: Both food lists place this bird among other winged creatures forbidden for eating. The lists do not describe its appearance or habits.

words.summary: Often rendered cormorant. The connection sometimes proposed with a bird plunging for prey is uncertain.

senses.definition: An oak or terebinth leaves a stump after felling. Isaiah uses the stump for the holy seed that remains.
The western gate on the ascending road marks one of the stations assigned to temple gatekeepers.

note: The gate bears the same form as the noun for felling. Chronicles gives no explanation of its name. Lane’s Arabic slk concerns following a road or threading, and does not establish the meaning throw or the older sound of shin here.
